summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, type II diabetes, chronic heart failure, and peripheral vascular disease was admitted after an uncomplicated fistulogram and angioplasty revealed episodes of narrow-complex tachycardia and long pauses on telemetry. He denied symptoms such as chest pain or dizziness, though his wife reported increased fatigue and sleep apnea symptoms. Evaluation showed sinus bradycardia with frequent premature atrial contractions in bigeminy and asymptomatic rhythm changes, likely influenced by procedural sedation and underlying cardiac disease. Hyperkalemia was identified and treated, with improvement in potassium levels following intervention and dialysis. His cardiac rhythm stabilized over the hospital stay, and he was discharged home with continued monitoring, medication adjustments, and follow-up arranged with cardiology and nephrology. No acute interventions such as pacemaker placement were required during this admission.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Chronic combined systolic and diastolic heart failure
Coronary atherosclerosis of unspecified type of vessel, native or graft
Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
